messages.content: Did my threshold test this morning. 20 minutes at 276W, so my FTP is now 262W.
Nice work. Logging FTP 262W from the 20 minute effort at 276W. That is a solid number to build from.
It is up from 255W back in March, so I am pleased with the progress.
A 7 watt gain since 255W in March is real progress. How did the effort pace out?
First few minutes too hot, faded slightly at the end. I also weighed in at 71kg today.
Noted, 71kg. I will recalc your zones around FTP 262W. Anything on the calendar we are aiming at?
Yes, the Alpine Gran Fondo on 1998-08-15. It is 168km with 3400m of climbing and I want to finish under 7 hours.
Great target. 168km and 3400m of climbing on 1998-08-15, under 7 hours. That course rewards steady climbing at sweet spot. What is your weekly availability?
I can train about 9 hours most weeks, and Tuesdays are always off for family.
Understood, 9 hours a week with Tuesdays off. I will structure the plan around that.
One caution: my left knee had patellar tendon trouble last autumn when I did three hard days in a row.
Important. I will cap you at two consecutive hard days to protect that left knee, and watch anything you report.
My indoor Kickr reads about 8W lower than my outdoor power meter, in case that is useful for targets.
It does. I will add the 8W offset so your indoor Kickr targets line up with outdoor numbers.
For structure, can we do a VO2max block and then a sweet spot build toward the Fondo?
Yes. Two weeks of VO2max work, then a sweet spot build into the Fondo. That fits the climbing demands.
This week, what does the long ride look like?
Let us do a 4.5 hour long ride on Sunday at endurance pace, keeping Tuesday off as always.
Sounds good. Should we retest FTP after the recovery week?
Good idea. We will retest FTP right after the recovery week to confirm the new number before the build.

facts.statement: goal event Alpine Gran Fondo on 1998-08-15, 168km with 3400m of climbing
trains about 9 hours per week, Tuesdays always off
left knee patellar tendon trouble last autumn from three hard days in a row; cap two consecutive hard days
indoor Kickr reads about 8W lower than the outdoor power meter
planned VO2max block then sweet spot build
athlete asked to retest FTP after the recovery week
